definitions: To arrive at a destination, especially a station or port.
To attract or draw in, often referring to customers or money.
To earn or acquire a certain amount of money.
To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop.
To take in or retract something, such as a part of one's body.
examples: The train will pull in shortly.
The new marketing campaign should pull in more clients.
He manages to pull in a good salary.
The police car pulled in behind us.
Pull in your stomach for the photo.
